status: Public source patch prerelease and website live; v0.1.6-alpha.1 release candidate verified

components.evidence_level: Public source patch prerelease; first physical kit recorded
components.checks: Full local hub check suite and kit freshness passed on the release candidate with gateway v0.1.0-alpha.5, Linux SDK v0.1.0-alpha.4, ESP32 SDK v0.2.0-alpha.7 and Home Assistant v0.1.0-alpha.4. The simulator kit is unchanged from v0.1.5-alpha.1. On 12 October the owner's ESP32-S3 + 1.3-inch SH1106 OLED kit passed physical acceptance, and Grok Bot showed text on it through local shell execution; native Grok Bot MCP calls are not claimed.

components.evidence_level: Simulated; Grok Bot local-command route observed
components.checks: 158 tests, Ruff, package builds, twine check and the demo passed. Adds the request log, named MCP tokens, per-token limits and the owner-run tunnel guide. On 12 October Grok Bot ran approved local rehearse commands and the request log recorded them; native Grok Bot MCP calls, the tunnel route and physical hardware are not verified.
54 tests, Ruff, package builds and the README quick start passed. The gateway integration used v0.1.0-alpha.4 with mcp 2.3.0. No fresh Linux container, systemd or Raspberry Pi run in this release.

components.evidence_level: Host simulated; three firmware examples compiled; OLED kit physically accepted on one board
components.checks: tools/check.sh host suites, the three firmware builds (atoms3-lite-usb, esp32s3-led-button, esp32s3-oled-kit) and the contract transcripts passed. On 12 October 2026 the owner observed the OLED kit firmware on a YD-ESP32-23 v1.3 board with an SH1106 OLED: text, clear, rejected text, RGB light, BOOT events, unplug/replug and gateway restart (docs/verification/oled-kit-2026-10-12.md). Disconnect during a command was not tested.
27 tests, Ruff and package builds passed; the fixture probe reports zero tool calls and resource reads. No real Home Assistant installation or Grok Bot connection was tested.
